title: Risk-cube reprice seam — dependency inverted through ExoticLegPricer (arch item E)
description: celnet-risk-cube no longer links the heavy pricers: it depends only on the celnet-core::carry::ExoticLegPricer abstraction (NOT celnet-exotics / celnet-gpu). The concrete exotic closed forms are injected into the cube as the server's ExoticEngine, which implements ExoticLegPricer, and the risk values are byte-identical across the inversion. This is the frozen-contract acceptance for the deliverable 'risk-cube-repricer-seam'.

assertions.statement: The server's ExoticEngine implements celnet_core::carry::ExoticLegPricer (unit_price + digital_greeks) — the concrete exotic closed forms (over celnet-exotics) are the injected reprice impl, satisfied via an IMPLEMENTS edge to the trait.

celnet-risk-cube's exotic reprice/curvature paths (exotic_curvature_legs, exotic_node_pnl, node_var_es_combined) depend on the celnet_core::carry::ExoticLegPricer abstraction via USAGE edges, never on a concrete pricer — the cube reprices a leg only through the injected trait object.

celnet-risk-cube's Cargo manifest lists NEITHER celnet-exotics NOR celnet-gpu (production or dev); the heavy pricers reach the cube only via the injected ExoticLegPricer. Gate: `cargo tree -p celnet-risk-cube` shows no celnet-exotics / celnet-gpu (manifest-level, not the symbol graph, which carries name-collision USAGE noise).
Risk-cube values (FRTB / VaR roll-ups) are byte-identical (to_bits) before and after the dependency inversion — the seam injects the same closed form, so the numbers are unchanged.
